tier_reason: Upgraded from C. RVV commit e1f49d9 (author date 2026-09-01) reports the in-tree benchmark test/affine-bench.c with exact command lines (taskset -c 2 ./test/affine-bench -b 0.8660254 -0.5 0.5 0.8660254 and -b 1 0.25 0.25 1), GCC 15.2.0, a Meson release build (buildtype=release, i.e. -O3, plus -march=rv64gcv1p0 for pixman-rvv.c from the public meson.build) and a SpacemiT K3 CPU, against the previous tree's generic C bilinear affine fetch, as medians of five interleaved runs. The SSE2 and NEON rows the record led with are first-party 2011 commit messages without compiler, flags or exact CPU, so on their own they are tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: RVV a8r8g8b8 bilinear affine fetch (commit e1f49d9, 2026-09-01) against the generic C fetch of the previous tree, SpacemiT K3, GCC 15.2.0, Meson release build, medians of five interleaved runs: affine-bench rotate 30 degrees 29.15 to 44.74 MPix/s (+53.48%), shear 0.25 36.46 to 60.75 MPix/s (+66.62%). Pure-scale lowlevel-blt-bench -b -c src_8888_8888 stays within run-to-run variation (-0.29% to +1.19%), because pure scaling was already served by the two-row-cache bilinear cover fetch. Follow-up commit caa79f2 (2026-09-24, K3 X100 core pinned to CPU 2 at 2.2 GHz) reports none-repeat affine a8r8g8b8 scale 0.5 75.24 to 119.36, rotate 30 28.41 to 42.53 and shear 0.25 34.56 to 55.87 MPix/s against the previous tree, with a forced-C build faster than RVV below widths of about 52-54 pixels. Historical first-party rows: SSE2 bilinear scaled src_8888_8888 (commit 3500293, 2011-02-21) is 'approximately 2x faster than pixman general compositing path'; its microbenchmark (2000x2000 image, scale factor close to 1x, Intel Core i7) goes from 70.48 to 165.38 MPix/s (2.35x, derived from page data), and cairo-perf-trace image firefox-planet-gnome from 12.566 to 10.961 (1.15x, derived from page data; the page gives no unit, though cairo-perf-trace prints its min and median columns in seconds). ARM NEON on a Cortex-A8: src_8888_8888 6.70 to 44.27 MPix/s (17feaa9), src_8888_0565 6.56 to 61.65 MPix/s (2ee27e7, r2p2 at 1 GHz with 32-bit LPDDR at 200 MHz), src_0565_x888 3.39 to 36.82 MPix/s (29003c3).
corrections.workload: Primary row: test/affine-bench, SRC compositing of a8r8g8b8 to a8r8g8b8 at 1920x1080 with bilinear filtering under a 30-degree rotation and a 0.25 shear (the default op and formats of affine-bench.c), pinned to one core. Historical rows: bilinear SRC compositing of a 2000x2000 image at a scale factor close to 1x (SSE2 a8r8g8b8 to a8r8g8b8 on x86-64; NEON 8888, 0565 and x888 variants on a Cortex-A8), plus a cairo-perf-trace replay of firefox-planet-gnome on the image backend.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Primary row: GCC 15.2.0, Meson release build (buildtype=release, i.e. -O3 without debug info; pixman-rvv.c gets -march=rv64gcv1p0 from meson.build). The 2011 SSE2 and NEON rows give no compiler or flags.
corrections.hardware: Primary row: SpacemiT K3 (RISC-V 64-bit with RVV 1.0; the follow-up commit caa79f2 names an X100 core pinned to CPU 2 at 2.2 GHz). Historical rows: an Intel Core i7 of unstated model (SSE2) and an ARM Cortex-A8 (NEON; r2p2 at 1 GHz with 32-bit LPDDR at 200 MHz in two commits).
corrections.caveats: Tier A rests on the RVV commit e1f49d9: the benchmark is in-tree (test/affine-bench.c), the command lines, compiler, build type and CPU are stated, and the runs are interleaved medians. 'Release build' is a Meson build type, not a literal flag list; it maps to -O3 under Meson's documented buildtype, and pixman's meson.build supplies -march=rv64gcv1p0 for the RVV file. The baseline is the previous tree, where rotated and sheared bilinear sources fall back to the generic C fetch (the existing bilinear cover iterators cover pure scaling only). The generic C file is built for the toolchain's default ISA, the usual runtime-dispatch setup, so the gain mixes hand-written RVV with any loss of autovectorization in the default build. The gain is about 1.5-1.7x on RISC-V; at row widths under about 52-54 pixels a forced-C build beats RVV (caa79f2). caa79f2's affine table uses a test-only affine-bench variant that is not in the tree. The SSE2 and NEON rows are first-party Nokia commit messages from 2011 (Siarhei Siamashka). The x86 CPU is given only as 'Intel Core i7', there is no compiler or flags, and the microbenchmark tool is unnamed; the 'op=1, src=..., dst=..., speed=' output does not match the in-tree lowlevel-blt-bench format. The 2011 baseline was the general compositing path of that time; later changes such as the SSSE3 bilinear iterator may have narrowed or moved the gap, so those ratios are historical. The NEON messages do not say that 'before' is the general C path; this is inferred from the diffs, which only add fast-path table entries and scanline functions. No SSSE3 fast-path-against-generic numbers were found. The aarch64 NEON commit (eadb828) points to freedesktop bug 94758, which was not opened. No independent third-party benchmark was found. gitlab.freedesktop.org failed from this environment (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so every page opened is the X11Libre/mirror.fdo.pixman GitHub mirror (described as a 'Read-only mirror for CI'; upstream gitlab.freedesktop.org/pixman/pixman.git). COPYING describes MIT as the license 'agreed upon by most contributors'; some files carry older permissive X11/HPND-style notices (for example test/affine-bench.c).

notes: All numbers check out verbatim against the mirror's commit messages (3500293, 17feaa9, 2ee27e7, 29003c3, e1f49d9); the derived ratios 2.35x and 1.15x are correct. I upgraded the entry to A on the 2026 RVV commit (in-tree affine-bench, GCC 15.2.0, Meson release, SpacemiT K3, interleaved medians against the generic C fetch), so the record's name no longer matches its primary row. Consider a name override such as 'pixman (SIMD bilinear fast paths: SSE2, NEON, RVV)'. The license (MIT, COPYING), last commit 2026-10-02 and active status are confirmed on the mirror. If the orchestrator does not accept a Meson build type as stated flags, the entry falls back to C.
